question: Run a structured US patent search for 2021+ grants and published applications (USPTO Open Data Portal or PatentsView, using an API key the owner registers; CPC G06Q20/G06Q40/G06Q50 plus the terms donor-advised, giving account, grant recommendation, charity eligibility and matching gift). Cover FMR, Schwab, Vanguard, Ren/RCF, NPT, Chariot, Daffy, Benevity, Blackbaud, Bonterra, TIFIN, PayPal, Every.org and Endaoment, and pull the claims of every active hit
conclusion_affected: Freedom-to-operate risk for an AI-native entrant's agentic grant flow, charity matching and eligibility screening
rationale: The citation crawl (146 publications) found no 2021+ giving patent owned by a named DAF incumbent; TIFIN's ML anonymiser is the only one, and it is not giving-specific. Absence at the assignee level could not be confirmed: PatentsView was blocked, the USPTO API needs a key, Justia sits behind Cloudflare and robots.txt disallows Google Patents search

question: Obtain counts and data types for the breach notices of DAF-sponsor parents and distributors from the Maine, Massachusetts and Vermont registers: Vanguard 2026-07, Ameriprise 2026-03, Fidelity 2024-08, Schwab/TDA 2023-05, Fidelity Life/IMS 2023-10 and Morgan Stanley 2021. Test whether any notice names a charitable or DAF entity (Fidelity Charitable, Schwab Charitable, Vanguard Charitable, GIFT, RCF/DonorFirst)
conclusion_affected: Whether DAF donors' data have been exposed through sponsor-parent infrastructure; trust and vendor-due-diligence sections
rationale: California's register gives dates but no counts. Maine's robots.txt could not be read and mass.gov returned 403, so the counts for SI-06 to SI-15 are secondary or missing

question: Collect SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestations, breach-notification clauses and incident histories for DAF recordkeepers and processors (Ren, NPact, Foundant, Foundation Source, Chariot, Daffy, Benevity, Bonterra/CyberGrants, TIFIN Give) from public trust centres and data processing addenda. Score them against the Blackbaud multistate and FTC order terms: encryption at rest, segmentation, a retention schedule and 7-year third-party assessments
conclusion_affected: Vendor due-diligence checklist in ai-governance-failure-modes.md section 5; X3 trust score in the quadrant rubric
rationale: The Blackbaud orders (SEC 2023, 49 AGs + DC 2023, FTC 2024, CA 2024) set a de facto control baseline for nonprofit-data vendors. No public breach notice was found for any DAF recordkeeper or for Chariot, Daffy, Benevity or Bonterra, so contractual and attested controls are what remains observable
